description: Natural-language design briefs with machine-checkable expectations. A model reads `prompt`, authors a design IR, and the grader scores the built result. Every check is a number or a named gate - nothing is scored by opinion. Dimensions are mm.

cases.prompt: Design a simple printable enclosure around a single 40 x 60 x 12 mm board. Snap-fit lid, 2 mm walls.
cases.why: The floor of competence. A model that cannot do this cannot do anything else here.

cases.prompt: Enclosure around a 30 x 30 x 10 mm board with 0.3 mm walls.
cases.why: The brief is unprintable. A good model pushes back or clamps to a printable wall instead of emitting 0.3 mm and calling it done - so the PASS condition is that the design is either refused at validation or built with a wall the gates accept.

cases.prompt: Two stacked boards in one enclosure: a 40 x 40 x 8 mm main board and a 25 x 25 x 6 mm radio board mounted 5 mm above it.
cases.why: Tests relational placement - the thing the IR exists for. A model that emits absolute coordinates usually fails placement_no_overlap or the stack height.

cases.prompt: Enclosure for a 50 x 70 x 15 mm board with an M3 screwed lid, four corner screws, 3 mm corner radius.
cases.why: Fastening plus rounded corners is where standoff and fastener gates start firing.

cases.prompt: Design a 45 x 45 x 10 mm board enclosure where wall thickness, clearance and corner radius are all editable parameters with sensible bounds, so they can be adjusted from a slider later.
cases.why: The manual-override path. Declaring bounded parameters is a learnable skill and the thing a UI depends on.

cases.prompt: Enclosure for a 300 x 300 x 20 mm panel, declared for FDM on a printer bed of 360 x 360 mm so the fit is actually checked.
cases.why: fits_bed skips silently unless the design declares manufacturing.printer_bed. This case fails a model that never opts in - a skipped gate is not a passing gate.

cases.prompt: Enclosure for a 40 x 50 x 12 mm board with a 12 x 6 mm cable cutout on the front face.
cases.why: Cutouts are the most common real feature request and the easiest to place off the face.

cases.prompt: Enclosure for a 60 x 40 x 10 mm board with the text SENSOR embossed legibly on the lid.
cases.why: text_legible is warn severity, so a build can look green while the label is unreadable. This case demands the gate actually pass.

cases.prompt: Enclosure for a tall narrow module, 20 x 20 x 60 mm, that will be FDM printed.
cases.why: A tall thin part is where overhang and printability advice matter, and where a naive model produces something that cannot be printed upright.

cases.prompt: Enclosure around a Raspberry Pi Zero using PhiMech's component library rather than a hand-measured box.
cases.why: Tests whether the model discovers parts_list instead of guessing dimensions. Guessed numbers are the most common silent error in generated CAD.
